items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: when I was studying classical bass with Rheinschagen

ctx.x: Debussy? It was so long -- when I was young, (inaudible) what I listened to. (Inaudible) Bach, I never heard too much Bach when I was young. But I changed my direction when I heard (inaudible). Heard Richard Strauss, "Death and Transfigurations", Stravinsky, which I like very much, but I still like Debussy better, for my own kind of music. I (inaudible) Stravinsky, but if I had to choose between the two, I would choose Debussy.

I keep saying Ellington, although I didn't come into Ellington until after I come into Debussy. Because I was hanging with a piano player named Spaulding Givens when I was studying classical bass with Rheinschagen. He opened my ears to these other composers. We were thinking about being classical composers when we were young. We never knew there was anything in jazz, because DownBeat magazine was a thing that only covered New York musicians -- still is, I think, it's very prejudiced to the whole field of jazz,…

Coast. I haven't read a DownBeat for years, but I see every from Buddy Collette body collect what he's doing. You go in the studios, I'm told PLAYING DOWN THERE. Leonard Feather (inaudible). I saw that the last time I was on the Coast, with Phil Moore, and I was wondering why he doesn't write about the guys all over America. The book is so narrow, a few that danced out here guys (inaudible) in the cold, snow and the blizzards and rain. These are the only ones that (inaudible) get accepted by DownBeat.
